texts.small-study.references:
1. Harbord test: Harbord, R. M., Egger, M., & Sterne, J. A. C. (2006). A modified test for small-study effects in meta-analyses of controlled trials with binary endpoints. Statistics in Medicine, 25(20), 3443-3457. doi:10.1002/sim.2380.
2. Arcsine asymmetry test: Rucker, G., Schwarzer, G., & Carpenter, J. R. (2008). Arcsine test for publication bias in meta-analyses with binary outcomes. Statistics in Medicine, 27(5), 746-763. doi:10.1002/sim.2971.
3. Additive random-effects regression: Thompson, S. G., & Sharp, S. J. (1999). Explaining heterogeneity in meta-analysis: A comparison of methods. Statistics in Medicine, 18(20), 2693-2708.
4. Peters test: Peters, J. L., Sutton, A. J., Jones, D. R., Abrams, K. R., & Rushton, L. (2006). Comparison of two methods to detect publication bias in meta-analysis. JAMA, 295(6), 676-680. doi:10.1001/jama.295.6.676.
5. Funnel plot axis choice: Sterne, J. A. C., & Egger, M. (2001). Funnel plots for detecting bias in meta-analysis: Guidelines on choice of axis. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 54(10), 1046-1055. doi:10.1016/S0895-4356(01)00377-8.
6. Implementation reference: Viechtbauer, W. (2010). Conducting meta-analyses in R with the metafor package. Journal of Statistical Software, 36(3), 1-48. doi:10.18637/jss.v036.i03.
texts.small-study.method-details:
Harbord test
  Package: meta 8.5-0
  Predictor: Harbord Z/V on 1/sqrt(V), where V is the native score variance
  Weighting: native Harbord score variance V
  Inference: t-based meta::metabias test
  Degrees of freedom: 10.00
  Exact p-value: 0.0048716477
  Call: meta::metabin(event.e, n.e, event.c, n.c, sm='OR', incr=0.5, method.incr='only0', common=TRUE, random=TRUE, method.tau='REML', level=0.95); meta::metabias(x=prepared.OR.model, method.bias='Harbord', k.min=10, level=0.95)

Rücker AS+RE test
  Package: meta 8.5-0
  Predictor: ASD effect on native ASD standard error
  Weighting: native AS+RE additive REML weights
  Inference: t-based meta::metabias test
  Degrees of freedom: 10.00
  Exact p-value: 0.033386308
  Call: meta::metabin(event.e, n.e, event.c, n.c, sm='ASD', common=TRUE, random=TRUE, method.tau='REML', level=0.95); meta::metabias(x=prepared.ASD.model, method.bias='Thompson', k.min=10, level=0.95)

Peters test
  Package: meta 8.5-0
  Predictor: 1/(n.e+n.c), with native Peters seTE=sqrt(1/(event.e+event.c)+1/(non-events.e+non-events.c))
  Weighting: 1/Peters seTE^2
  Inference: t-based meta::metabias test
  Degrees of freedom: 10.00
  Exact p-value: 0.0000098577722
  Call: meta::metabin(event.e, n.e, event.c, n.c, sm='OR', incr=0.5, method.incr='only0', common=TRUE, random=TRUE, method.tau='REML', level=0.95); prepared.OR.model$TE <- prepared.effects; prepared.OR.model$seTE <- prepared.standard.errors; meta::metabias(x=prepared.OR.model, method.bias='Peters', k.min=10, level=0.95)

texts.Clinical interpretation:
Across 17 studies, summary sensitivity was 65.76% (95% confidence interval 59.02% to 71.92%) and summary specificity was 80.97% (95% confidence interval 73.88% to 86.49%).
These are average operating characteristics across the included study thresholds. The Reitsma bivariate and HSROC formulations are equivalent parameterizations of this model; that equivalence does not assume a common threshold. Use the prediction intervals to assess how performance may vary in a new setting.
